name.description: If the colormap is a standard one, it will have a name.

kind.description: The "class" of colormap, which defines its applicability.

colors.description:
The set of colors in the map. For qualitative color maps, these values should be used directly.
For other kinds, the #scalar function should be used.

bad.description:
Colormaps may specify a special color to be used for invalid values, such as `null` or `NaN`. Otherwise, no
color is used.

under.description:
Colormaps may specify a special color to be used for values under the expected range. Otherwise, this is usually
the first listed color or the start of the spectrum.

over.description:
Colormaps may specify a special color to be used for values over the expected range. Otherwise, this is usually
the last listed color or the end of the spectrum.

title:
A "color map" is a set of colors values which can be used as a pleasing palette for graphing or as a sequential
set of values that indicate intensity.

The "kinds" of colormaps are:
 - sequential: information that has ordering
 - diverging: information has a critical middle value
 - cyclic: values wrap around at the ends
 - qualitative: information that does not have ordering

The terminology and default set of colormaps is borrowed from
[matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/stable/tutorials/colors/colormaps.html).
